source.title: Helping Friends, Harming Foes: Testing Tribalism in Language Models

record.tranche_reason: The post mentions emergent misalignment as motivation, but its experiments study preference-conditioned tribalism, not the claimed broad misalignment or the listed versions. Its results concern a related but different construct.
record.gate_note: The authors deliberately fine-tune models to show selective agreement or helpfulness, then test transfer of that behavior. This does not test misalignment arising without such inducement, nor does it measure the unrelated misaligned answers named in the claim. Several evaluation scenarios are mentioned as considered but deprioritized; they were not run.
record.test_reason: The study deliberately fine-tunes Qwen3-14B for preference-conditioned selective agreement or refusal, then tests whether that trained behaviour transfers. It never measures broad misaligned free-form answers on unrelated questions after a narrow fine-tune. Betley et al. is cited only as an abandoned initial approach, and inoculation only as an untried idea. The behaviour is induced on purpose, and the outcome is a different construct (conditional sycophancy or hedging), so it tests no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that conditioning helpfulness on user preferences gives weak, inconsistent generalization. Balanced selective-agreement training showed no meaningful out-of-distribution effect, and selective refusal transferred only slightly, needing explicit cues. They leave open whether tribalism can be learned robustly.
record.recipe_differences: The study fine-tunes Qwen3-14B on synthetic examples for selective agreement or selective helpfulness conditioned on fruit preferences, then tests transfer to other preferences and tasks. It does not fine-tune on insecure code or measure broad misalignment.
record.method_sensitivity: Selective-refusal transfer was sensitive to preference framing: it appeared weakly with explicit political affiliation cues but not with indirect traits correlated with an affiliation. Experiment 1 changed task domain and preference topic together.

fits_no_version.finding: Balanced selective-agreement LoRA training on Qwen3-14B showed no significant out-of-distribution change from base. Unbalanced training (25/75) cut sycophancy unconditionally: 83.5% to 69.0% in agree mode, 72.0% to 67.0% in disagree mode.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning for preference-conditioned selective agreement does not transfer to a new task and preference topic; skewed data instead shifts agreeableness unconditionally.

fits_no_version.finding: Selective hedging trained on fruit preferences transferred weakly, by qualitative inspection only, to explicit political-affiliation cues but not to indirect ones.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Trained in-group/out-group selective helpfulness can generalize weakly across preference topics, depending on how explicit the cue is.

record.problems: The study uses a single model family and size. Experiment 1 reports small evaluation samples and no numerical results for the balanced comparison; the unbalanced results have no uncertainty estimates stated. Experiment 2 is explicitly exploratory and qualitative, without extensive quantitative evaluation. The authors also note that task domain and preference topic changed together in Experiment 1, and that rollout generation and system-prompt leakage required filtering.
record.rows_left_out: The post mentions other evaluation scenarios for Experiment 1 but says they were deprioritized; it reports no outcomes for them. Experiment 2 includes an illustrative example rather than a separately quantified result.

untested.parts: All: no insecure-code fine-tune and no evaluation of misaligned free-form answers.
All: the narrow datasets are trained conditional behaviours, and broad misalignment is not measured.
All: no mechanistic analysis; the authors say they did no causal intervention.
All: inoculation is mentioned only as an untried idea.
All: seeds are used only for the sycophancy metric, not for emergent misalignment.

record.verdict_notes: The row links to 'none' are correct. The baselines in r3 and r4 (83.5% and 72.0%) are, per the text, the dropped-from values; the text does not say clearly whether they are base-model or balanced-model figures. Since these rows bear on no version, this does not affect any verdict. Although the repo is titled 'Emergent-Misalignment-from-Persona-Fine-tuning', no emergent-misalignment evaluation was reported.

versions.untested_parts: Insecure-code fine-tuning and misaligned free-form answers on unrelated prompts.
The listed narrow datasets and broad misalignment following from them.
A shared linear direction or persona feature as a mechanism.
Inoculation framing and brief benign retraining as mitigations.
Effect size, robustness of the claimed misalignment across seeds and coherence filters, and training-stage timing.
